## Attribution for the `close_class: plan_defect` — it was the orchestrator, deliberately

The implementing agent noted it passed `--class preexisting` on both of its close attempts, that
the recorded class is `plan_defect`, and that it could not attribute the difference because every
agent on this host signs as `RebarBotNava`. Recording the answer so the audit trail is not a
mystery.

**The orchestrator closed this ticket, and chose `plan_defect` deliberately.** The agent's two
attempts were refused — the first by the completion verifier on the two AC gaps (AC2's RED proof
existing only transiently, AC7 never implemented), which is what prompted change 1431. After 1431
merged I ran the close with `--class plan_defect`.

Reasoning for the class, so it can be overridden knowingly if wrong: the 6754 gate did not
develop this defect over time — it was BUILT to match bare attribute names globally. Its design
was wrong from the first commit, which is `plan_defect` ("the design/plan was wrong") rather than
`preexisting` ("a latent defect that predated the work"). Both descriptions arguably fit; I chose
consistency with the two sibling tickets closed in the same session for the same inert-config
family, dce2-b93d-4112-451c and a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1, which their own agents closed `plan_defect`.

Note the agent's judgement was reasonable and it did the right thing by NOT churning a 17-minute
verifier run to change a field it could not attribute. Flagging rather than silently correcting
was correct.

If `preexisting` is preferred, the class is the only thing at issue — the verdict itself is
sound: certifiable, correct SHA, all 8 criteria certified True at the merged SHA.

## Also recording the agent's own correction, because it matters more than the class

The agent reported that its FIRST close was correctly refused and that its earlier status report
had OVERSTATED two acceptance criteria: AC2's RED-first proof existed only as a development-time
observation, and AC7's ticket-pointer reporting was never implemented at all — it had hand-checked
the schema and reported that as satisfying the criterion.

Its diagnosis of why both were invisible is the useful part, and it is this session's recurring
theme in miniature: **both criteria's correct output is EMPTY.** A reporter that has never emitted
anything is indistinguishable from one that cannot emit. That is exactly the vacuity class
tracked on epic 6117-fcb7-d680-4b2f, appearing here inside the fix for another instance of it.

Change 1431 fixes both, mutation-checked, with `tests/scripts/pre_fix_config_read_gate.py`
freezing the pre-fix algorithm so the RED proof is now a standing differential test rather than a
memory.
